traits.height_max_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923), as Thuya plicata: reaches a maximum height of 60 m to 70 m. Sargent (1922) says frequently 200 ft (60.96 m); Silvics vol. 1 cites a very large Washington tree of 54.3 m.

traits.wood_modulus_green_mpa.note: Wood Handbook 2021 (FPL-GTR-282), table 5-3a, Cedar, western red, green: modulus of elasticity 6,500 MPa in static bending (clear wood, centre-loaded, span 14 depths; specific gravity 0.31).

traits.wood_rupture_green_mpa.note: Wood Handbook 2021 (FPL-GTR-282), table 5-3a, Cedar, western red, green: modulus of rupture 35,900 kPa (clear wood in static bending).

traits.wood_moisture_green_share.note: Wood Handbook 2021 (FPL-GTR-282), table 4-1, Cedar, western red: average moisture content of green wood, heartwood 58% and sapwood 249% of oven-dry mass; stated as a share, the range between them with its middle typical where both are given.

traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 species aggregate for Thuja plicata (gwddagg_v2.2_species.csv, read): specific gravity 0.34 (wsg_est, the database's hierarchical-model species mean, from 11 records in 8 sources); trunks 0.32, branches 0.47. Basic density (oven-dry mass over green volume) is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

traits.cone_posture.note: FEIS's western redcedar review: cones clustered near the twig ends, turned up on short stalks. Read with Abrams's strongly reflexed cones on hanging sprays: they point up.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams (vol. 1, 1923, p. 71), as Thuya plicata: scale leaves about 3 mm (FEIS: 1.5 to 3 mm), twice that on leading shoots; the branchlets usually fall in their third year, taking their leaves; seed cones 10 to 12 mm, clustered near the branch ends and strongly bent back.

traits.leaf_life_years.note: Harlow, Duursma and Marshall (2005, abstract) aged the scale leaves of 26 dominant and codominant redcedars in northern Idaho by the growth rings where they fall: 8.9 years on average, about 6.8 in the upper third of the crown and 10.6 in the lower third. Abrams (1923, p. 71) has the branchlets falling in their third year, taking their leaves; that is the small side branchlets the tree sheds, not how long a leaf lives, so the measured span replaces his.

traits.cone_length_m.note: Abrams (vol. 1, 1923, p. 71), as Thuya plicata: scale leaves about 3 mm (FEIS: 1.5 to 3 mm), twice that on leading shoots; the branchlets usually fall in their third year, taking their leaves; seed cones 10 to 12 mm, clustered near the branch ends and strongly bent back.

traits.juvenile_period_years.note: FEIS (Tesky 1992, read): seed production normally begins at 20 to 30 years, but open-grown trees may produce seed by age 10. The Woody Plant Seed Manual (Thuja, read): trees as young as 10 years have produced cones. It sets adult_age through the rule at the seed plants (spec rework P6), in place of the 15 years set by hand.

generator.params.note: Hand-set for a western redcedar: a leader that nods over and straightens, branches that sweep down and turn up at the tips, flat scale-leaved sprays hanging below them, foliage kept about five years. Spray area matched to the drawn sprays. Not fitted to data. Cones (plant forms F3): about 1 cm, upright, in clusters; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Spec rework E6d: `cone_length`, `cone_pitch`, `needle_years` now set by the rules at Pinidae from the stated characters. Conifer form (pinidae revision 5): `branch_reach` fitted so the open-grown crown keeps revision 4's radius at the oldest keyframe.

allometry.note: Rough heights and diameters for redcedar in a mixed western Washington stand, from general forestry knowledge: slower in height than Douglas-fir. Replace with a published site-index table before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: yellow-green foliage, red-brown fibrous bark in twisting strips, a fluted, buttressed base. Bark pattern (plant roadmap P4, `bark_pattern`): stringy grey to reddish-brown bark in long fibrous strips; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.seed_length_m.note: Idžojtić, Dendrology (2019) p. 674, Thuja plicata: seed length 4-5 mm.
